items.title: Global systematic review of how climate change degrades the wellbeing and health of Indigenous children.

ai.headline: Climate change is linked to poorer health and wellbeing among Indigenous children worldwide.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 53 studies found that climate change is linked to adverse health outcomes in Indigenous children, including effects on psychosocial and cultural wellbeing, malnutrition, infectious diseases, perinatal health, and morbidity and mortality. Heat exposure and seasonal and hydroclimatic variability were the most frequently reported climate exposures.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how environmental changes can affect the health and cultural wellbeing of children in Indigenous communities around the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how changes in weather and seasons affect your own mood, energy, and daily routines.
ai.fact: Indigenous children across diverse global contexts are experiencing adverse climate-related health outcomes.

quiz.question: What were the most frequently linked climate exposures in the review?
quiz.answer: Heat exposure and seasonal and hydroclimatic variability were the most frequently linked climate exposures.

ai.caveat: The studies were heterogeneous and meta-analysis was not feasible, so findings are narrative rather than pooled statistics.

items.title: Education and training interventions for healthcare workers to prevent sexual harassment.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Training may slightly improve knowledge and skills for preventing sexual harassment among healthcare workers.
ai.summary: This Cochrane review looked at education and training to prevent sexual harassment in healthcare settings. Two studies involving 170 nurses found that training probably slightly increases prevention knowledge and may slightly improve management skills, but no study measured whether harassment actually decreased.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that while training can build awareness, there is no evidence yet that it stops harassment from happening.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether workplace training actually changes behaviour, not just what people know.
ai.fact: Sexual harassment among healthcare workers is linked to poor mental health, job dissatisfaction, and people leaving their jobs.

quiz.question: Did the review find evidence that training reduces the incidence of sexual harassment?
quiz.answer: No, none of the included studies measured the incidence of sexual harassment.

ai.caveat: The review is based on only two small studies of nurses in Taiwan, and both compared different types of training rather than training versus no training.

items.title: Pre-sleep alpha-lactalbumin and dietary protein interactions on sleep, mood, and cognition in athletes with sleep difficulties: a protocol for a factorial crossover randomised controlled trial

ai.headline: A trial will test whether a milk protein supplement improves sleep, mood and thinking in athletes who sleep poorly.
ai.summary: This study protocol describes a planned randomised crossover trial in 24 athletes with sleep difficulties. It will compare alpha-lactalbumin, a whey protein from cow’s milk, with a placebo under two different dietary protein conditions, measuring sleep, mood and cognition.
ai.why_it_matters: It could show whether a simple whole-food supplement helps athletes sleep better and recover more effectively.

quiz.question: What is the main aim of the planned trial?
quiz.answer: To investigate whether alpha-lactalbumin supplementation improves sleep, mood and cognition in athletes with sleep difficulties.

ai.caveat: This is only a study protocol, so no results have been collected or analysed yet.

items.title: A Critical Epistemological Audit of Early Evidence Syntheses in Generative AI Educational Research: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

ai.headline: Early reviews of ChatGPT in education show mixed, uncertain results because the underlying studies vary widely in quality.
ai.summary: Researchers audited five early meta-analyses covering 87 studies on ChatGPT’s effects in education. They found a positive average effect, but results varied greatly and weakened when stricter quality checks were applied, especially for studies measuring actual learning rather than performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why a single headline number about AI in education should not be taken as proof of a stable, general benefit.
ai.life_skill: Check whether claims about educational tools are based on high-quality, transparent research before relying on them.
ai.fact: Most early studies assessed performance exclusively, while only a small share assessed learning exclusively.

quiz.question: What did the reconstructed meta-analysis find about the average effect of ChatGPT on educational outcomes?
quiz.answer: It found a positive average effect, but the results varied substantially and became weaker under stricter quality checks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Informal carers’ experiences of mental health services regarding supporting those they care for and getting support for their own wellbeing: A systematic umbrella review of qualitative evidence

ai.headline: Informal carers often face exclusion, distress and barriers when using mental health services for themselves or the person they support.
ai.summary: This umbrella review combined findings from twelve qualitative reviews about unpaid carers’ experiences of mental health services. It found that while some carers had positive experiences, most described exclusion, emotional distress and structural barriers to getting support for themselves or the person they care for.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how mental health services can affect not only service users but also the family and friends who support them.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether services are involving and supporting you as a carer, and ask for information about carer support if you are not being included.
ai.fact: Informal carers include family members, friends or other unpaid supporters of people with mental health difficulties.

quiz.question: What did most carers describe in their experiences of mental health services?
quiz.answer: Most described exclusion, emotional distress and structural barriers to support.

ai.caveat: The findings come from qualitative reviews of carers’ experiences, so they show patterns of reported experience rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: The psychosocial impacts of skin-neglected tropical diseases (SNTDs) as perceived by the affected persons: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Skin neglected tropical diseases cause serious mental and social harm, especially for women.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 27 qualitative studies on people living with skin neglected tropical diseases such as leprosy and cutaneous leishmaniasis. Most participants reported stigma, avoidance, abandonment, low mood, anxiety and reduced ability to work or socialise, with women generally facing worse social consequences.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how visible illness can damage mental health and social participation, highlighting the need for supportive communities and early treatment.
ai.life_skill: Notice if someone with a visible skin condition is being avoided and offer ordinary, respectful contact.
ai.fact: Skin neglected tropical diseases are linked to stigma, low mood, anxiety and reduced social participation.

quiz.question: Which group generally experienced worse social consequences from skin neglected tropical diseases?
quiz.answer: Women generally experienced worse social consequences than men.

ai.caveat: The review only included qualitative studies published in English, so findings may not apply to all settings or languages.

items.title: Human-Centered GenAI Feedback Design in Higher Education: A Multisite Experiment on Direct, Reflective, and Hybrid Approaches to Scientific Argumentation
items.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

ai.headline: GenAI feedback works best when students stay in charge of their own learning
ai.summary: A multisite experiment with 1,176 first-year science students compared peer-only, direct AI, reflective AI, and hybrid feedback. Direct AI feedback improved argument quality most quickly, but reflective and hybrid designs led to better uptake, self-regulated learning, conceptual learning, and delayed AI-free transfer.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how AI feedback is designed matters more than simply having access to AI, especially for lasting learning.
ai.life_skill: When using AI feedback, pause to judge and revise the work yourself rather than just accepting the AI's suggestions.
ai.fact: Feedback designs that preserve student agency and evaluative judgment can support better delayed learning than direct AI feedback alone.

quiz.question: Which feedback condition showed the clearest advantage on conceptual learning?
quiz.answer: The hybrid condition combining self-evaluation, peer feedback, and GenAI critique yielded the highest adjusted mean for immediate argument-quality gain and showed the clearest advantage on conceptual learning.

ai.caveat: This is a single multisite field experiment in introductory university science courses, so results may not apply to all subjects, ages, or settings.

items.title: Quantifying Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Using Artificial Intelligence-Based Matching

ai.headline: AI can quickly match cancer patients to clinical trials using structured rules.
ai.summary: Researchers built an AI tool that turns cancer trial eligibility rules into computer code and checks synthetic patient records against them. It matched 746 trials in under half a second per patient and agreed with doctors on 95.8% of patient-trial pairs.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI might one day help people find suitable cancer trials faster, though it is not yet ready for real patient use.

quiz.question: What did the AI tool convert trial eligibility criteria into?
quiz.answer: It converted them into Structured Query Language (SQL) code for rule-based matching.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and used synthetic patient vignettes rather than real patients.

items.title: The 4th Trimester Initiative: The Impact of Parental Support on Pregnant Trainee Wellbeing

ai.headline: A trial is testing whether mentorship, sleep and lactation support improves trainee mothers’ wellbeing and reduces medical errors.
ai.summary: This randomised trial compares new trainee mothers given extra support—including a smart bassinet, breast pump, perinatal care access and a faculty mentor—against those receiving standard support. Researchers will measure burnout, professional fulfilment, sleep, medical errors, breastfeeding goals and postpartum depression using surveys and Fitbit data.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace support during pregnancy and early parenthood may affect both personal wellbeing and patient safety.
ai.life_skill: Notice what support your workplace or training programme offers new parents and ask about mentorship or flexible options if you need them.
ai.fact: The study will compare an intervention group receiving mentorship, lactation and sleep support with a control group receiving standard support.

quiz.question: What are researchers comparing in this trial?
quiz.answer: They are comparing trainee mothers given extra parental support with those receiving standard support to see if wellbeing improves and medical errors decrease.

ai.caveat: Results are posted on a trial registry and have not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not confirmed.

items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering

ai.headline: A new AI agent can train itself to do machine-learning engineering tasks more effectively.
ai.summary: Researchers developed MLExpert, a 35-billion-parameter AI agent, using a post-training method that learns from intermediate results across long machine-learning experiments. On MLE-Bench Lite, its average medal rate rose from 37.9% to 72.7%, matching larger frontier models, and it also improved on related tasks such as NatureBench Lite and algorithm optimization.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI systems might increasingly automate complex technical work, which could change how software and AI are built in the future.
ai.life_skill: Try breaking a long project into smaller steps and reviewing the result of each step before moving on.
ai.fact: MLExpert is a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model trained for autonomous machine-learning engineering.

quiz.question: What happened to MLExpert's average medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite compared with the base model?
quiz.answer: It improved from 37.9% to 72.7%.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the results come from benchmark tests rather than real-world deployment.

items.title: Predictive Multi-Objective Energy--Latency Optimization in Cloud Environments Using Ensemble Learning

ai.headline: AI can cut cloud data centre energy use while keeping response times stable.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a predictive system that learns how much energy servers use and how long requests wait, then chooses settings to save energy without delays. On real cloud traces, it cut energy by up to 72.4 percent versus running servers at full speed, with no stability violations and low latency.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how cloud services could use less electricity while still responding quickly, which matters for the cost and environmental impact of the digital tools people use every day.
ai.life_skill: Notice which apps or devices you leave running when you do not need them, and close or turn them off to save energy.
ai.fact: Cloud data centres must balance energy use against communication delay, and this trade-off is strongly coupled and nonlinear.

quiz.question: What did the energy-only minimisation approach have that the gradient-boosting controller did not?
quiz.answer: Energy-only minimisation had 3.80 percent stability violations, while the gradient-boosting controller had zero violations.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the results come from trace-driven emulation rather than a live cloud deployment.

items.title: Associations of self-reported physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health among civil aviation flight students: a cross-sectional study

ai.headline: More vigorous activity and more sleep are linked to better mental health in male flight students.
ai.summary: A survey of 776 civil aviation flight students looked at physical activity, sitting time, sleep, and mental health. Among men, longer vigorous activity was linked to lower anxiety, sleeping under 7 hours was linked to higher depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic internet use, and more sitting time was linked to more problematic internet use.

items.title: Judging strangers' preferences may actually be easier when they're less like our own

ai.headline: Judging strangers is easier when they differ
ai.summary: Researchers studied how people understand others' preferences. They found that using one's own preferences as a starting point may not always be effective. This challenges the idea of egocentric anchoring being the best approach.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how we judge others' preferences can help us improve our relationships and interactions with people who are different from us.
ai.life_skill: Try to consider alternative perspectives when judging others' preferences.
ai.fact: Humans have a tendency to use egocentric anchoring to understand others.

quiz.question: What cognitive bias do people use to understand others?
quiz.answer: Egocentric anchoring.

ai.caveat: This finding is based on a news report and may not be supported by peer-reviewed evidence.
